newsitem.title: NIGERIA: African force says it is ready for Liberia poll.
newsitem.headline: African force says it is ready for Liberia poll.

text.p: The West African ECOMOG force in charge of peacekeeping in Liberia is well deployed nationwide for elections in the country, its commander said on Monday.
West African leaders last week postponed to July 19th Liberia's presidential and legislative elections originally scheduled for May 30, for security and logistics reason.

"We in ECOMOG are totally ready for the elections," Major-General Sam Victor Malu, the commander of the Nigerian-led troops, told a news briefing in Lagos, adding: "ECOMOG is convinced that the security situation would allow for elections to be held nationwide.
"With our deployment in all population centres, we would easily move troops to other additional centres where elections would hold if so desired by the election commission," he said.
The 10,954-strong force in February completed the disarming of Liberia's civil war factions, effectively ending the war which erupted in 1989.
The war killed more than 150,000 people and turned half the pre-war population of 2.5 million into refugees in neighbouring countries.
Malu said refugees and displaced persons were steadily returning home and urged Liberian political parties to take their electioneering campaigning to the hinterland.
"Many of the villages in the interior of Liberia that were desolate when ECOMOG troops were first deployed in February and March are now bubbling back to life," he said.
He said the force had been greatly strengthened by recent logistic support from Western nations, among them the United States, Britain and Germany.
"By the time ECOMOG is leaving Liberia, the country will be more arms-free than many members of the Economic Community of West African States," he said.
According to him more than 30,000 former faction fighters had been disarmed by ECOMOG and large quantities of arms and ammunition seized.
